channel.title: NewsCenter — Top 5 news of the day — 2026-11-27
channel.description: The five news that matter most today, chosen from Laurent's newsletters. 108 news received.

item.title: 1. Nvidia Suspends Server Shipments to Southeast Asia
item.description: Why it matters: Nvidia’s reported halt of server shipments to four Southeast Asian markets shows that tighter U.S. export controls are already disrupting regional data-center investment and supply chains. Nvidia reportedly asked server manufacturers to halt deliveries to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia after new U.S. export rules took effect. Fitch expects slower growth and more selective investment in the region’s data centers.

item.title: 2. Dell reaches $22 billion in revenue from AI servers
item.description: Why it matters: Dell’s $22 billion in AI-server revenue and $132.3 billion backlog demonstrate the exceptional scale of enterprise demand—and the growing risk of delivery constraints—for AI infrastructure. Dell generated $22 billion in AI-server revenue, up 291%. Its order backlog reached $132.3 billion, which could delay some deliveries.

item.title: 3. SAP Considers Cutting at Least 10,000 Jobs in AI-Related Restructuring
item.description: Why it matters: SAP’s potential elimination of at least 10,000 jobs signals how major software companies are restructuring their workforces and costs around AI adoption. The job cuts would affect about 9% of SAP’s global workforce. The final number still depends on negotiations with employee representatives.

item.title: 4. 42 Attorneys General Oppose the Sale of Character.AI Conversations
item.description: Why it matters: The bipartisan push by 42 attorneys general to block the sale of Character.AI conversation histories could establish important precedents for consumer-data ownership, deletion rights and AI privacy enforcement. A bipartisan coalition of 42 U.S. attorneys general is trying to block the planned sale of conversation histories from more than 21 million accounts. It criticizes the lack of safeguards allowing users to delete data or requiring buyers to follow privacy policies.

item.title: 5. Investigation finds undisclosed AI use in 25 court cases
item.description: Why it matters: Undisclosed AI-generated errors in at least 25 English and Welsh court cases highlight immediate risks to institutional trust and could accelerate rules requiring transparency and human oversight in legal work. The Bureau of Investigative Journalism found undisclosed AI use in at least 25 cases in England and Wales. Some rulings included fabricated case law and nonexistent statutes.
